limitations: One registered workspace, one session and one observed ACP child per fresh run; no concurrent-child capacity conclusion.
The fixed read-only count covers case-sensitive literal occurrences in tracked non-binary files. The execution protocol differs from v1; results are not pooled.
Every target page was compared with archived fixture text, proving normalized text delivery through ACP. This does not establish understanding or cross-turn retention.
Count answer JSON is verified. Other final prose is retained but not semantically graded.
Old-generation/live-set peaks are lifetime maxima including startup. GC deltas span before-first-turn to before-teardown, including settling, without forced GC.
Paired prompt latency is observational; model output and tool sequences can differ, so it does not isolate heap overhead.
No claim about long sessions, multi-session, multi-MCP, concurrent children, Node 24, other host partitions, RSS limits or safe production capacity.
Production enforcement remains unimplemented and must wait for broader calibration.

independentFinalAudit.protocolInterpretation: Only the heavy counting turn requires exactly one fixed Shell invocation. File turns require every frozen page to match, while extra read-only calls are reported separately. The initial audit mistakenly required exactly 23 tools per heavy run; its failed result is preserved in matrix-independent-audit-strict-first-pass.json.
limitations: This matrix observes one workspace/session/ACP child per run, not production admission enforcement or concurrent capacity.
Both light files and three heavy files are compared with frozen fixture payloads when that profile is present; summary semantics are not graded.
Counter output and answer match the separately archived independent byte-counter oracle; its 419 source files were not all downloaded or independently recounted by this audit.
Permission evidence is the collector original report record linked by toolCallId, not a second raw permission event stream.
GC deltas include between-turn and final settling waits; heap maxima cover the complete process lifetime.
Cleanup is verified from archived owned-process checks and daemon tail, without a new remote process query.
File turns may perform additional read-only checks beyond the required pages; their varying work precludes attributing paired wall-time differences solely to heap ceiling.
